rationale: Multiple independent multicenter and familial studies (Miyamoto et al., Hengel et al., Roller et al., Mouraux et al.) demonstrate that the recurrent heterozygous switch II missense variant p.Arg83Trp in RAB3A causes autosomal dominant spinocerebellar ataxia 52 (SCA52), characterized predominantly by adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia with variable pyramidal features (gait spasticity) and tremors. While other variant types (such as loss-of-function or non-switch-II missense alleles) and occasional early-onset cases associate with neurodevelopmental delay or infantile onset, the assertion that p.Arg83Trp specifically produces an adult-onset progressive cerebellar ataxia syndrome with mild spasticity and tremor—rather than being exclusively an infantile/congenital non-progressive encephalopathy—is firmly supported.

evidence.text: Miyamoto and colleagues identified the heterozygous c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp) variant in the conserved switch II region of RAB3A in two families with autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia. Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar ataxia, accompanied by mild spasticity and tremors, alongside cerebellar cortical atrophy accentuated in the vermis.

source.title: An R83W mutation in Rab3A causes autosomal-dominant cerebellar ataxia
source.quote: In this study, we identified the c.247C > T p.(Arg83Trp) variant in RAB3A, encoding a small GTPase involved in membrane-associated regulated exocytosis, in two families with cerebellar ataxia. Affected individuals presented with adult-onset, gradually progressive cerebellar symptoms, often accompanied by mild gait spasticity and tremors.

numbers.metric: Number of families identified with c.247C>T p.(Arg83Trp)

evidence.text: Hengel et al. screened rare disease databases and cohort datasets, identifying 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families who shared a cerebellar ataxia phenotype. Nine of the 10 families harbored the recurrent p.Arg83Trp variant. Separate de novo or loss-of-function variants were linked to distinct neurodevelopmental presentations.

source.title: Heterozygous RAB3A variants cause cerebellar ataxia by a partial loss-of-function mechanism
source.quote: In total, we identified 18 individuals from 10 unrelated families all sharing a cerebellar ataxia phenotype. Notably, 9 of the 10 families carried a recurrent variant in RAB3A, p.Arg83Trp, including one de novo occurrence. In addition, our screening revealed three families with a neurodevelopmental phenotype and three unique RAB3A variants, which were either de novo or loss-of-function variants.

evidence.text: Roller et al. explored the phenotypic spectrum of the recurrent RAB3A R83W variant across nine unrelated families presenting with pure cerebellar ataxia and spasticity, situating this hot-spot mutation within the progressive ataxia-spasticity spectrum.

conflicts: While p.Arg83Trp predominantly leads to progressive adult-onset cerebellar ataxia with pyramidal signs, Miyamoto et al. reported variable neurodevelopmental features in some family members, and Hengel et al. linked distinct loss-of-function and non-hotspot variants to congenital neurodevelopmental presentations.

new_directions.question_text: What specific genetic or environmental modifiers explain the presence of neurodevelopmental symptoms in a subset of p.Arg83Trp carriers compared to those presenting with isolated adult-onset cerebellar ataxia?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying why some individuals carrying the p.Arg83Trp variant show mild developmental manifestations alongside adult-onset neurodegeneration will refine diagnostic differentiation and prognostic counseling.

new_directions.question_text: Does the biochemical disruption of effector coupling (e.g., RIM1 and Rabphilin-3A binding) by p.Arg83Trp differ qualitatively or quantitatively from the partial loss-of-function seen in infantile-onset RAB3A variants?
new_directions.rationale: Mapping allele-specific synaptic docking and exocytosis deficits across the switch II versus other functional domains will explain the genotype-phenotype divergence between progressive SCA52 and congenital ataxic encephalopathies.
